extraction.body: Two off-duty FBI agents intervened to help an off-duty police officer who was working security when he was attacked by a suspect who had accosted a female customer at the Walmart in Waukegan. Esteban Martinez-Cruz, 18, of North Chicago, was charged with aggravated battery of a peace officer, two counts of battery and resisting a peace officer. Lake County Assistant State’s Attorney Sue Price Cohen said a Randall, Wisconsin, police officer was off-duty and working security at Walmart, 3900 Fountain Square Place in Waukegan, on April 21. He was wearing a blue shirt that had “security” written on it and was wearing a police badge and had a service weapon. An employee of the store informed the security officer that a female customer reported that Martinez-Cruz had his hand in his pants and was waving at her to follow him, Price Cohen said. Martinez-Cruz was told to leave by the employee but got aggressive in the employee’s face and allegedly pushed him. The two began wrestling on the ground and the security guard intervened and tried to control Martinez-Cruz, Price Cohen said. Martinez-Cruz wrestled with the security guard as he tried to handcuff him. Price Cohen said Martinez-Cruz escaped and then slammed the victim to the ground, injuring his ribs. Two off-duty FBI agents, who were customers of the store, intervened and helped detain Martinez-Cruz, who was highly intoxicated, Price Cohen said. The Lake County State’s Attorney’s Office did not file a petition to detain Martinez-Cruz because the offenses are non-detainable under the Illinois SAFE-T Act. Lake County Judge Randi Bruno released Martinez-Cruz, saying she had no authority to hold him despite the allegations. “I have to release you on conditions,” the judge said. Martinez-Cruz was placed on Level 3 pre-trial supervision and ordered to undergo random drug and alcohol screenings. He was additionally ordered not to possess any weapons. He was also ordered to have no contact with any of the people involved in the incident and not go to the Walmart in Waukegan. Martinez-Cruz, who is reportedly a senior in high school, is scheduled to appear in court again on June 4 for a status of preliminary hearing. © 2026 SJB Business Solutions, Inc. ISSN No. 2769-4283. sources.title: Off-duty officer attacked while running on Wildwood boardwalk; group arrested
passages: WILDWOOD, N.J. - Five suspects have been arrested and charged with the unprovoked attack of an off-duty police officer at the Jersey Shore last week.
sources.body: WILDWOOD, N.J. - Five suspects have been arrested and charged with the unprovoked attack of an off-duty police officer at the Jersey Shore last week.

extraction.body: WILDWOOD, N.J. - Five suspects have been arrested and charged with the unprovoked attack of an off-duty police officer at the Jersey Shore last week. An off-duty Stone Harbor officer was assaulted while he was out on an evening run on the Wildwood boardwalk. The victim suffered signigicant injuries, including a concussion and facial fractures. Officials say the unprovoked attack was carried out by a group who had traveled from Gloucester and Camden counties. All five suspects were arrested, and have been identified as Isaiah Ortiz, 19; Elijah Williams, 19; William Jewell, 20; Manuel Ortiz, 21; and Maliky Reyes, 20. Isaiah Ortiz and Elijah Williams were remanded to the Cape May County Correctional Facility for aggravated assault and related offenses. The other three suspects were charged with failure to remand aid to a victim and released on a summons. "We will continue to work tirelessly to hold those accountable for their actions and ensure that justice is served for the victim," said Cape May County Prosecutor Sutherland. Isaiah Ortiz and Elijah Williams both face up to 10 years in state prison. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX Television Stations

extraction.body: A security guard tells FOX 5 he thought he was going to die, describing an incident outside a Prince George’s County nightclub, that landed an off-duty D.C. Investigators said the off-duty officer used his police Glock in that altercation. Download the FOX 5 DC News App for Local Breaking News and Weather"You want to kill me? You say you want to murder me?" is what Mohamed Sesay said he shouted toward off-duty D.C. Police Officer, Dennis Sfoglia. It was around 2:30 in the morning on May 6 when Prince George’s County Police responded to Spectrum Lounge in Beltsville, Maryland for a fight.Mohamed Sesay told FOX 5 he works for a Baltimore-based company, hired by Spectrum to work security. That morning, Sesay claimed Sfoglia placed him in a choke hold and threatened his life."He grabbed me and the girlfriend was also on my hand. And he took, grabbed me, scold me like this [showing his hand around his neck] and took the gun and point it right into my stomach," said Sesay, who then described the off-duty officer as saying, "I will kill you, shoot you. I will shoot you in the stomach, what do you have to say?" "I said, leave me, I cannot breathe," the security guard told FOX 5. The security guard said he started recording once that choke hold was released.In the video you see someone who appears to be off-duty D.C. Police Officer Dennis Sfoglia wearing an MPD badge around his neck. The off-duty officer has a handgun out with the firearm at his side and pointed toward the ground. His index finger can be seen sitting along-side the barrel, not on the gun’s trigger.It’s difficult to make-out what is being said to Sesay, but in the video you can clearly hear the security guard shout, "You’re holding a gun, I’m recording you!" Sesay told FOX 5 he was not armed. Court documents say the whole incident started after the off-duty officer’s girlfriend got into an argument with at least one other woman over a missing passport. Sesay said the girlfriend had used a passport as identification to get into the club. At one point, the girlfriend reportedly became irate. Court documents said she began to cause damage inside the lounge. The security guard then removed her, claiming he picked her-up from underneath her arms. Sfoglia told Prince George’s County Police he went to break up that altercation, and in court documents, admitted to taking out his firearm and pointing it toward the ground. Multiple witnesses told police that’s when Sfoglia approached Sesay, grabbed his neck and pointed his gun toward the security guard. Court documents also noted the Glock was found with 15 bullets in the magazine and one bullet in the chamber.DC Police confirmed for FOX 5 on Friday, Sfoglia was placed on no-contact status. Police Chief Robert Contee told FOX 5 he recommended indefinite suspension. "He has a right to appeal that decision but that’s the recommendation that’s been put forward – indefinite suspension," said Contee. It’ll be addressed," said the Chief when asked what his message to the community is. FOX 5 was unable to reach Sfoglia.In response to FOX 5’s request, the D.C. Police Union President wrote, "Just like every defendant, this member is innocent until proven guilty. He has asserted that these charges are false and that once the facts are heard, he will be wholly exonerated. He is currently represented by an attorney and any further questions should be directed to his counsel."Sfoglia was previously recognized by the department for helping to save a man while off-duty as a recruit. He also previously faced trouble for posting racially-insensitive content online. The off-duty officer is due back in court in June, facing charges of First and Second Degree Assault along with the Use of a Firearm in a Violent Crime. SUBSCRIBE TO FOX 5 DC ON YOUTUBEIt was not made immediately clear in Maryland court information who the attorney representing Sfoglia is.

extraction.body: Two off-duty FBI agents intervened to help an off-duty police officer who was working security when he was attacked by a suspect who had accosted a female customer at the Walmart in Waukegan. Esteban Martinez-Cruz, 18, of North Chicago, was charged with aggravated battery of a peace officer, two counts of battery and resisting a peace officer. Lake County Assistant State’s Attorney Sue Price Cohen said a Randall, Wisconsin, police officer was off-duty and working security at Walmart, 3900 Fountain Square Place in Waukegan, on April 21. He was wearing a blue shirt that had “security” written on it and was wearing a police badge and had a service weapon. An employee of the store informed the security officer that a female customer reported that Martinez-Cruz had his hand in his pants and was waving at her to follow him, Price Cohen said. Martinez-Cruz was told to leave by the employee but got aggressive in the employee’s face and allegedly pushed him. The two began wrestling on the ground and the security guard intervened and tried to control Martinez-Cruz, Price Cohen said. Martinez-Cruz wrestled with the security guard as he tried to handcuff him. Price Cohen said Martinez-Cruz escaped and then slammed the victim to the ground, injuring his ribs. Two off-duty FBI agents, who were customers of the store, intervened and helped detain Martinez-Cruz, who was highly intoxicated, Price Cohen said. The Lake County State’s Attorney’s Office did not file a petition to detain Martinez-Cruz because the offenses are non-detainable under the Illinois SAFE-T Act. Lake County Judge Randi Bruno released Martinez-Cruz, saying she had no authority to hold him despite the allegations. “I have to release you on conditions,” the judge said. Martinez-Cruz was placed on Level 3 pre-trial supervision and ordered to undergo random drug and alcohol screenings. He was additionally ordered not to possess any weapons. He was also ordered to have no contact with any of the people involved in the incident and not go to the Walmart in Waukegan. Martinez-Cruz, who is reportedly a senior in high school, is scheduled to appear in court again on June 4 for a status of preliminary hearing. © 2026 SJB Business Solutions, Inc. ISSN No. 2769-4283. extraction.body: WILDWOOD, N.J. - Five suspects have been arrested and charged with the unprovoked attack of an off-duty police officer at the Jersey Shore last week. An off-duty Stone Harbor officer was assaulted while he was out on an evening run on the Wildwood boardwalk. The victim suffered signigicant injuries, including a concussion and facial fractures. Officials say the unprovoked attack was carried out by a group who had traveled from Gloucester and Camden counties. All five suspects were arrested, and have been identified as Isaiah Ortiz, 19; Elijah Williams, 19; William Jewell, 20; Manuel Ortiz, 21; and Maliky Reyes, 20. Isaiah Ortiz and Elijah Williams were remanded to the Cape May County Correctional Facility for aggravated assault and related offenses. The other three suspects were charged with failure to remand aid to a victim and released on a summons. "We will continue to work tirelessly to hold those accountable for their actions and ensure that justice is served for the victim," said Cape May County Prosecutor Sutherland. Isaiah Ortiz and Elijah Williams both face up to 10 years in state prison. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX Television Stations

Labat said the two men left the store, but returned around 11 p.m. and that’s when the situation turned violent. Authorities arrested 29-year-old Xavier Evans and his younger brother, 24-year-old Xavion Evans. Both are being held without bond on felony charges of aggravated assault resulting in serious bodily injury and aggravated battery against a law enforcement officer, according to jail records. The injured detention officer has launched a GoFundMe campaign to help offset costs as he recovers. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

extraction.body: A security guard tells FOX 5 he thought he was going to die, describing an incident outside a Prince George’s County nightclub, that landed an off-duty D.C. Investigators said the off-duty officer used his police Glock in that altercation. Download the FOX 5 DC News App for Local Breaking News and Weather"You want to kill me? You say you want to murder me?" is what Mohamed Sesay said he shouted toward off-duty D.C. Police Officer, Dennis Sfoglia. It was around 2:30 in the morning on May 6 when Prince George’s County Police responded to Spectrum Lounge in Beltsville, Maryland for a fight.Mohamed Sesay told FOX 5 he works for a Baltimore-based company, hired by Spectrum to work security. That morning, Sesay claimed Sfoglia placed him in a choke hold and threatened his life."He grabbed me and the girlfriend was also on my hand. And he took, grabbed me, scold me like this [showing his hand around his neck] and took the gun and point it right into my stomach," said Sesay, who then described the off-duty officer as saying, "I will kill you, shoot you. I will shoot you in the stomach, what do you have to say?" "I said, leave me, I cannot breathe," the security guard told FOX 5. The security guard said he started recording once that choke hold was released.In the video you see someone who appears to be off-duty D.C. Police Officer Dennis Sfoglia wearing an MPD badge around his neck. The off-duty officer has a handgun out with the firearm at his side and pointed toward the ground. His index finger can be seen sitting along-side the barrel, not on the gun’s trigger.It’s difficult to make-out what is being said to Sesay, but in the video you can clearly hear the security guard shout, "You’re holding a gun, I’m recording you!" Sesay told FOX 5 he was not armed. Court documents say the whole incident started after the off-duty officer’s girlfriend got into an argument with at least one other woman over a missing passport. Sesay said the girlfriend had used a passport as identification to get into the club. At one point, the girlfriend reportedly became irate. Court documents said she began to cause damage inside the lounge. The security guard then removed her, claiming he picked her-up from underneath her arms. Sfoglia told Prince George’s County Police he went to break up that altercation, and in court documents, admitted to taking out his firearm and pointing it toward the ground. Multiple witnesses told police that’s when Sfoglia approached Sesay, grabbed his neck and pointed his gun toward the security guard. Court documents also noted the Glock was found with 15 bullets in the magazine and one bullet in the chamber.DC Police confirmed for FOX 5 on Friday, Sfoglia was placed on no-contact status. Police Chief Robert Contee told FOX 5 he recommended indefinite suspension. "He has a right to appeal that decision but that’s the recommendation that’s been put forward – indefinite suspension," said Contee. It’ll be addressed," said the Chief when asked what his message to the community is. FOX 5 was unable to reach Sfoglia.In response to FOX 5’s request, the D.C. Police Union President wrote, "Just like every defendant, this member is innocent until proven guilty. He has asserted that these charges are false and that once the facts are heard, he will be wholly exonerated. He is currently represented by an attorney and any further questions should be directed to his counsel."Sfoglia was previously recognized by the department for helping to save a man while off-duty as a recruit. He also previously faced trouble for posting racially-insensitive content online. The off-duty officer is due back in court in June, facing charges of First and Second Degree Assault along with the Use of a Firearm in a Violent Crime. SUBSCRIBE TO FOX 5 DC ON YOUTUBEIt was not made immediately clear in Maryland court information who the attorney representing Sfoglia is.

passages: Apple has set 13 October for a ‘Welcome home’ launch, and the rumours all point to smart home hardware.
In a post on X, Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, teased the company’s next reveal with a short video and four words: “Welcome home.
Invitations have also gone to some members of the press for an “Apple Experience” in Tribeca, New York, starting at 9:00 a.m.
ET on 13 October, as shared by Marques Brownlee .
9to5Mac notes that Apple ran a similar hands-on session for the MacBook Neo earlier this year.
Welcome home. October 13. pic.twitter.com/ChelGSDOTI
9to5Mac also expects the LG-made smart lock and thermostat that leaked recently to appear, since Apple reportedly co-developed them with LG.
MacRumors says the hub has been ready for months and was waiting on Siri AI, which TechRadar notes arrived last month with iOS 27.
The launch also follows our look at the three Apple launches to watch this month .
Apple hasn’t said where the products will go on sale, or at what price.
Pricing so far is a US rumour only, so there is no UAE figure to cite yet.
Everything below comes from rumours and code leaks, not Apple.

passages: 빠른 답변 Apple이 2026년 10월 13일 ‘Welcome home’ 신제품 공개를 공식 확인했습니다. 초대장에 따르면 뉴욕 트라이베카에서 Apple Experience가 열리며 시작 시간은 미국 동부시간 오전 9시. 주목할 제품은 신형 Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, 그리고 HomePad로 불리는 스마트 홈 디스플레이입니다. 이후 10월 말에는 Mac과 iPad 4개 제품군이 추가 공개될 것으로 보도됐지만, 해당 라인업은 Apple이 확인하지 않았습니다. 구매를 미룰 수 있다면 Apple TV나 HomePod mini를 사기 전에 10월 13일 발표를 확인하세요.

October 13.” MacRumors: 10월 13일 제품 공개 공식 발표 MacRumors: 10월 13일 스마트 홈 프리뷰 MacRumors: 10월 말 MacBook Pro·iPad mini 공개 보도 MacRumors: iPad mini 60Hz OLED 소문 Apple Newsroom: iPhone Duo 사전 주문 및 출시일 자주 묻는 질문 Apple 10월 13일 이벤트는 공식 확정됐나요? 네.
10월 13일 공개가 예상되는 Apple 신제품은? 가장 유력한 예상은 스마트 홈 제품 3종입니다. 각 제품의 공식 발표와 최종 사양은 아직 공개되지 않았습니다.
Apple 월드와이드 마케팅 수석부사장 Greg Joswiak은 “Welcome home.

Mac mini 알루미늄 액세서리 ZEERA MacFrost Pro Mac mini 액티브 쿨러 30W TEC 냉각 CNC 알루미늄 OLED 모니터링 3가지 냉각 모드 M6 / M5 Pro / M4 제품 보기 ZEERA MacForge Gen3 CNC 알루미늄 Mac mini 케이스 Mac Pro 그릴 CNC 섀시 향상된 공기 흐름 SSD 확장 전면 포트 제품 보기 지금 살까, Apple의 10월 발표를 기다릴까?

Apple 기기에 추천 ZEERA MagTri Gen2: 액티브 쿨링 탑재 25W Qi2.2 접이식 MagSafe 충전기 ZEERA MagTri Gen2는 iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods를 위한 접이식 3-in-1 MagSafe 충전 액세서리입니다. 호환 iPhone에 최대 25W Qi2.2 무선 충전을 제공하며, 장시간 충전 시 열을 관리하는 액티브 쿨링 시스템을 갖췄습니다. 접으면 작아져 책상, 침대 옆, 여행지에서 Apple 기기 3대를 한 충전 스테이션에 정리할 수 있습니다. 지금 구매 2026년 10월 9일 업데이트. 아래에서는 공식 일정과 보도·예상 제품 정보를 구분해 설명합니다.
Bloomberg 보도를 정리한 10월 8일 MacRumors 기사에 따르면 미디어 체험 행사와 온라인 영상 발표가 함께 진행될 전망입니다. 시청 정보는 Apple Events 및 Apple 공식 채널에서 확인하세요. 초대장 시작 시간만으로 일반 공개 영상의 게시 시간을 확정할 수는 없습니다.

Apple HomePad: 완전히 새로운 스마트 홈 디스플레이? 흔히 ‘HomePad’로 불리는 Apple Home Hub는 홈 제어, FaceTime, 위젯, 개인 정보를 가족이 공유하는 디스플레이로서 가장 큰 신제품이 될 가능성이 있습니다. 보도에 따르면 약 6인치 화면, 벽걸이형과 스피커 베이스형, 가족 구성원에 맞춰 인터페이스를 바꾸는 카메라와 재실 센서를 갖춥니다. 약 350달러부터라는 전망이 있지만 Apple은 가격을 발표하지 않았습니다. 주방 캘린더, 복도 제어 화면, 가족용 통화 기기 등 실제 설치 위치를 생각해 보세요. 여러 대를 사기 전에 앱 지원, 계정 개인정보 보호, 설치 조건, 지원 언어를 확인해야 합니다.

extraction.body: Apple could be preparing to announce a new partnership with home security company ADT as part of its “Welcome home” product launch on Tuesday, October 13. MacRumors reports that a series of clues surrounding newly hired ADT technicians point toward a possible tie-up with Apple, potentially covering installation services for the company’s upcoming smart home products. The report comes just days before Apple’s home-focused launch, where the company is expected to introduce its long-rumored HomePad smart home hub alongside a new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. According to MacRumors, ADT has been hiring “Low Voltage Technicians” in several U.S. cities since around July, but some of those employees have reportedly been given few details about what their eventual role will involve. Some new hires are said to have spent recent months shadowing existing ADT technicians while waiting for further instructions, with employees and managers reportedly signing nondisclosure agreements connected to the role. Another clue is the hardware being issued to the new technicians. MacRumors says the employees have been provided with iPhones for work, while other ADT technicians typically use Android devices. Several of the new hires are also reportedly expecting to receive more information about their responsibilities later this month, potentially lining up with Apple’s October 13 announcements. The most obvious role for ADT would be professional installation. Apple is expected to introduce a wall-mounted version of HomePad, while the company is also reportedly working with LG on a wider ecosystem of connected-home products. The Apple Post reported this week on new iPhone proximity controls apparently being developed for the LG accessories, which are expected to include products such as security cameras, a video doorbell, thermostat and smart lock. MacRumors says some ADT employees have been told the secretive role will involve home automation and in-home installation services. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has set 13 October for a ‘Welcome home’ launch, and the rumours all point to smart home hardware.
In a post on X, Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, teased the company’s next reveal with a short video and four words: “Welcome home.
Invitations have also gone to some members of the press for an “Apple Experience” in Tribeca, New York, starting at 9:00 a.m.
ET on 13 October, as shared by Marques Brownlee .
9to5Mac notes that Apple ran a similar hands-on session for the MacBook Neo earlier this year.
Welcome home. October 13. pic.twitter.com/ChelGSDOTI
9to5Mac also expects the LG-made smart lock and thermostat that leaked recently to appear, since Apple reportedly co-developed them with LG.
MacRumors says the hub has been ready for months and was waiting on Siri AI, which TechRadar notes arrived last month with iOS 27.
The launch also follows our look at the three Apple launches to watch this month .
Apple hasn’t said where the products will go on sale, or at what price.
Pricing so far is a US rumour only, so there is no UAE figure to cite yet.
Everything below comes from rumours and code leaks, not Apple.

빠른 답변 Apple이 2026년 10월 13일 ‘Welcome home’ 신제품 공개를 공식 확인했습니다. 초대장에 따르면 뉴욕 트라이베카에서 Apple Experience가 열리며 시작 시간은 미국 동부시간 오전 9시. 주목할 제품은 신형 Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini 2, 그리고 HomePad로 불리는 스마트 홈 디스플레이입니다. 이후 10월 말에는 Mac과 iPad 4개 제품군이 추가 공개될 것으로 보도됐지만, 해당 라인업은 Apple이 확인하지 않았습니다. 구매를 미룰 수 있다면 Apple TV나 HomePod mini를 사기 전에 10월 13일 발표를 확인하세요.

October 13.” MacRumors: 10월 13일 제품 공개 공식 발표 MacRumors: 10월 13일 스마트 홈 프리뷰 MacRumors: 10월 말 MacBook Pro·iPad mini 공개 보도 MacRumors: iPad mini 60Hz OLED 소문 Apple Newsroom: iPhone Duo 사전 주문 및 출시일 자주 묻는 질문 Apple 10월 13일 이벤트는 공식 확정됐나요? 네.
10월 13일 공개가 예상되는 Apple 신제품은? 가장 유력한 예상은 스마트 홈 제품 3종입니다. 각 제품의 공식 발표와 최종 사양은 아직 공개되지 않았습니다.
Apple 월드와이드 마케팅 수석부사장 Greg Joswiak은 “Welcome home.

Mac mini 알루미늄 액세서리 ZEERA MacFrost Pro Mac mini 액티브 쿨러 30W TEC 냉각 CNC 알루미늄 OLED 모니터링 3가지 냉각 모드 M6 / M5 Pro / M4 제품 보기 ZEERA MacForge Gen3 CNC 알루미늄 Mac mini 케이스 Mac Pro 그릴 CNC 섀시 향상된 공기 흐름 SSD 확장 전면 포트 제품 보기 지금 살까, Apple의 10월 발표를 기다릴까?

Apple 기기에 추천 ZEERA MagTri Gen2: 액티브 쿨링 탑재 25W Qi2.2 접이식 MagSafe 충전기 ZEERA MagTri Gen2는 iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods를 위한 접이식 3-in-1 MagSafe 충전 액세서리입니다. 호환 iPhone에 최대 25W Qi2.2 무선 충전을 제공하며, 장시간 충전 시 열을 관리하는 액티브 쿨링 시스템을 갖췄습니다. 접으면 작아져 책상, 침대 옆, 여행지에서 Apple 기기 3대를 한 충전 스테이션에 정리할 수 있습니다. 지금 구매 2026년 10월 9일 업데이트. 아래에서는 공식 일정과 보도·예상 제품 정보를 구분해 설명합니다.
Bloomberg 보도를 정리한 10월 8일 MacRumors 기사에 따르면 미디어 체험 행사와 온라인 영상 발표가 함께 진행될 전망입니다. 시청 정보는 Apple Events 및 Apple 공식 채널에서 확인하세요. 초대장 시작 시간만으로 일반 공개 영상의 게시 시간을 확정할 수는 없습니다.

Apple HomePad: 완전히 새로운 스마트 홈 디스플레이? 흔히 ‘HomePad’로 불리는 Apple Home Hub는 홈 제어, FaceTime, 위젯, 개인 정보를 가족이 공유하는 디스플레이로서 가장 큰 신제품이 될 가능성이 있습니다. 보도에 따르면 약 6인치 화면, 벽걸이형과 스피커 베이스형, 가족 구성원에 맞춰 인터페이스를 바꾸는 카메라와 재실 센서를 갖춥니다. 약 350달러부터라는 전망이 있지만 Apple은 가격을 발표하지 않았습니다. 주방 캘린더, 복도 제어 화면, 가족용 통화 기기 등 실제 설치 위치를 생각해 보세요. 여러 대를 사기 전에 앱 지원, 계정 개인정보 보호, 설치 조건, 지원 언어를 확인해야 합니다.
Bloomberg 보도를 정리한 MacRumors 최신 기사 는 다음 공개 시점을 10월 27일 전후으로 봅니다. 이는 보도된 일정이며 Apple 공식 초대장이 아닙니다. 제품 변형에 따라 전체 수를 세는 방식도 달라질 수 있습니다.
Apple의 설명 전에는 휴대 사용, 전체 iPad App Store, 동일한 앱 호환성을 전제로 하지 마세요. 기존 HomePod도 같은 Siri AI 기능을 받나요? 기능별로 지원 여부가 다를 수 있습니다. 발표 후 Apple이 제시하는 지원 모델, 소프트웨어 버전, 언어, 지역을 확인하세요. iPad mini 8에 120Hz 화면이 탑재되나요?
HomePod 프로세서와 색상 전망은 제공된 영상 해설에도 나오지만 Apple의 공식 사양표는 아닙니다.
M6 iMac M6 iMac이 7번째 주목 제품군입니다. 영상은 대대적인 재설계보다 칩 중심 업데이트를 예상합니다. 데스크톱 구매 시 올인원인지, 컴퓨터와 모니터를 따로 살지 결정하세요.

Apple의 설명 전에는 휴대 사용, 전체 iPad App Store, 동일한 앱 호환성을 전제로 하지 마세요. 기존 HomePod도 같은 Siri AI 기능을 받나요? 기능별로 지원 여부가 다를 수 있습니다. 발표 후 Apple이 제시하는 지원 모델, 소프트웨어 버전, 언어, 지역을 확인하세요. iPad mini 8에 120Hz 화면이 탑재되나요?
HomePod 프로세서와 색상 전망은 제공된 영상 해설에도 나오지만 Apple의 공식 사양표는 아닙니다.
M6 iMac M6 iMac이 7번째 주목 제품군입니다. 영상은 대대적인 재설계보다 칩 중심 업데이트를 예상합니다. 데스크톱 구매 시 올인원인지, 컴퓨터와 모니터를 따로 살지 결정하세요.

passages: The 10-Year Treasury yield recently hit 5.3%, its highest level since 2007. As a result, issuers of CDs, bonds, and other fixed-income investments will need to raise their yields to stay competitive. That shift could draw investors away from stocks and other riskier investments.

Some investors might argue that Bitcoin ( BTC +0.90% ) is immune to that shift because it's becoming a safe-haven hedge against the debasement of fiat currencies. But at $84,000, Bitcoin remains about 33% below its all-time high of $126,000 from last October. Let's see why higher yields are weighing down Bitcoin -- and why it might bounce back if those yields decline.

Bitcoin is mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work ( PoW ) consensus mechanism, which relies on powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles. But every four years, a scheduled "halving" halves those rewards, making it even harder to mine Bitcoin profitably.

More than 20 million of Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million tokens have already been mined, but its increasing difficulty will prevent its last token from being mined until 2140. That scarcity makes it more comparable to gold than many other cryptocurrencies, so it's often considered a hedge against inflation and the devaluation of the U.S. dollar.

However, rising Treasury yields also usually drive investors away from gold. While gold might be a good hedge against a weakening dollar, rising yields actually strengthen the U.S. dollar. As that happens, it makes more sense for investors to shift from gold toward low-risk CDs, Treasuries, bonds, and other fixed-income investments that pay guaranteed interest. At the same time, rising borrowing costs will prevent investors from taking on riskier, leveraged bets and drive them to liquidate more volatile investments to fund their fixed-income purchases.

Bitcoin, as "digital gold," is exposed to the same headwinds. Many institutional investors will also rotate out of Bitcoin ETFs -- which provide exposure to Bitcoin without crypto wallets and keys -- as Treasury yields rise. So while Bitcoin and gold still might be good long-term bets against the U.S. dollar and other fiat currencies, they won't bounce back unless the Treasury yields cool off and risk-seeking investors return to the market.

I'm still bullish on Bitcoin's long-term growth potential, since monetary expansion policies will inevitably debase fiat currencies. But investors shouldn't conflate that debasement with the near-term pressures of rising interest rates and Treasury yields. Those challenges could prevent Bitcoin from revisiting its all-time highs for the foreseeable future.

STMicroelectronics (NYSE: STM) offers a broad portfolio of semiconductors across various industries and applications, and it's finding huge growth opportunities ahead in AI data centers and low earth orbit satellites. STMicro doesn't make the heavy-duty processors used for training and running AI. It makes key components for various applications, including power conversion and thermal management. Its biggest growth driver for its data center business, however, is its position in optical connectivity -- chips that enable AI servers to transmit data to one another. Management expects its data center segment to generate $1 billion in revenue in 2026 and to more than double that in 2027. That's a huge growth segment for a company that produced $11.8 billion in revenue last year. STMicro has been making chips for outer space operations since the 1970s. But its partnership with SpaceX to develop chips for use on its satellites and in its ground equipment has significantly increased its revenue in recent quarters. The company makes radio-frequency chips that help steer beams toward SpaceX satellites. It also makes a range of specialized chips for use in the satellites themselves. As SpaceX launches more satellites, STMicro expects its revenue related to the business to total $3 billion between 2026 and 2028. The company guided for $18 billion in revenue by 2028 at its Capital Markets Day in 2024. With the stronger-than-anticipated growth in both AI and space, it should be able to outperform that outlook. Additionally, it should be able to generate improvements in gross margin and operating income as demand for its chips continues to climb and it uses more of its manufacturing capacity. That should ultimately lead to a strong earnings cycle for the company through the end of the decade. The stock currently trades around 37 times forward earnings estimates, but that multiple will decline over the next few years as EPS is expected to nearly triple from this year through 2028. However, investors shouldn't expect the stock to move in lockstep with earnings growth, as the semiconductor stock can be extremely cyclical, pushing its earnings multiple much lower as earnings peak. STMicro doesn't make the heavy-duty processors used for training and running AI. It makes key components for various applications, including power conversion and thermal management.

Its biggest growth driver for its data center business, however, is its position in optical connectivity -- chips that enable AI servers to transmit data to one another. Management expects its data center segment to generate $1 billion in revenue in 2026 and to more than double that in 2027. That's a huge growth segment for a company that produced $11.8 billion in revenue last year.

STMicro has been making chips for outer space operations since the 1970s. But its partnership with SpaceX to develop chips for use on its satellites and in its ground equipment has significantly increased its revenue in recent quarters. The company makes radio-frequency chips that help steer beams toward SpaceX satellites. It also makes a range of specialized chips for use in the satellites themselves.

As SpaceX launches more satellites, STMicro expects its revenue related to the business to total $3 billion between 2026 and 2028. That outlook doesn't include any potential upside from SpaceX's plans for orbital data centers.

There's plenty of growth ahead across STMicro's portfolio. The company guided for $18 billion in revenue by 2028 at its Capital Markets Day in 2024. With the stronger-than-anticipated growth in both AI and space, it should be able to outperform that outlook. Additionally, it should be able to generate improvements in gross margin and operating income as demand for its chips continues to climb and it uses more of its manufacturing capacity. That should ultimately lead to a strong earnings cycle for the company through the end of the decade.
The stock currently trades around 37 times forward earnings estimates, but that multiple will decline over the next few years as EPS is expected to nearly triple from this year through 2028.

However, investors shouldn't expect the stock to move in lockstep with earnings growth, as the semiconductor stock can be extremely cyclical, pushing its earnings multiple much lower as earnings peak. Still, it looks much more attractive at its current price than SpaceX stock.

sources.title: SpaceX vs. Micron: Which Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Own for the Next 5 Years? - The Motley Fool
passages: Two of the more popular artificial intelligence (AI) stocks among investors right now are Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX +1.25% ) and Micron Technology ( MU -0.66% ) .
However, one clearly stands out as the better buy over the next five years: SpaceX.
That is why SpaceX is the better long-term bet, despite Micron trading at a much cheaper valuation on the surface.
If you want to invest in technological innovation and the future, SpaceX is one of your best options.
CEO Elon Musk has set a goal for SpaceX to reach $1 trillion in revenue in 2030.
Geoffrey Seiler has no position in any of the stocks mentioned.
The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Micron Technology.
SpaceX looks poised to outperform Micron in the coming years.
Let's look at why I'd buy SpaceX and avoid Micron.
SpaceX has some of the best economics in the entire data center space, getting returns on its AI infrastructure spending within one year through short-term leases.
With demand for compute so constrained, the company has been renting out its excess compute capacity at huge prices.
It has a $1.25 billion-per-month lease deal with Anthropic that runs through 2029, worth a total of $84.5 billion.
The company is investing aggressively in AI infrastructure, and expects to have total capacity near 2 gigawatts at the end of 2026 and closer to 10 gigawatts than 5 gigawatts at the end of 2027.
One of the big three DRAM (dynamic random-access memory) makers, Micron, has been riding the memory supercycle to new heights.
Soaring AI demand has led to surging memory prices, which have led to Micron's revenue skyrocketing and gross margin ballooning.
The current supply-demand imbalance in the DRAM market is expected to last through at least 2030, according to Micron rival SK Hynix .

A special form of DRAM called high bandwidth memory (HBM) is the main memory driver, as graphics processing units (GPUs) need to be packaged with the chips to optimize their performance; otherwise, these super-expensive chips sit around idle way too long.
Micron actually derives only a small percentage of its revenue from HBM, likely less than 10%.
It has the smallest HBM share in the market, at around 18% in Q2, in what is projected to be around a $55 billion market in 2026.

extraction.body: Two of the more popular artificial intelligence (AI) stocks among investors right now are Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX +1.25% ) and Micron Technology ( MU -0.66% ) . However, one clearly stands out as the better buy over the next five years: SpaceX. Let's look at why I'd buy SpaceX and avoid Micron. If you want to invest in technological innovation and the future, SpaceX is one of your best options. Meanwhile, over the next five years, the company's growth is likely to be driven mostly by leasing data center infrastructure, AI coding, and satellite internet. SpaceX has some of the best economics in the entire data center space, getting returns on its AI infrastructure spending within one year through short-term leases. With demand for compute so constrained, the company has been renting out its excess compute capacity at huge prices. It has a $1.25 billion-per-month lease deal with Anthropic that runs through 2029, worth a total of $84.5 billion. The company is investing aggressively in AI infrastructure, and expects to have total capacity near 2 gigawatts at the end of 2026 and closer to 10 gigawatts than 5 gigawatts at the end of 2027. In addition to its infrastructure-as-a-service business, the company has a huge opportunity with AI coding following its acquisition of Cursor. Morgan Stanley sees this as a $33 billion annual recurring revenue business by 2030, up from about $8 billion this year. The company's Starlink satellite internet business is also growing quickly, is profitable, and generates recurring revenue. Meanwhile, any advancements with its Starship rocket and future ventures, like putting data centers in space, should get investors excited. CEO Elon Musk has set a goal for SpaceX to reach $1 trillion in revenue in 2030. That's well above the current $421.7 billion consensus, so if it gets anywhere close to Musk's target, the stock will have significant upside over the next five years. One of the big three DRAM (dynamic random-access memory) makers, Micron, has been riding the memory supercycle to new heights. Soaring AI demand has led to surging memory prices, which have led to Micron's revenue skyrocketing and gross margin ballooning. Both DRAM (73% of Micron's revenue last quarter) and NAND (flash) are in short supply, which is driving up prices. The current supply-demand imbalance in the DRAM market is expected to last through at least 2030, according to Micron rival SK Hynix . The reason is that the three companies that control the DRAM market, including Samsung , can't increase capacity fast enough to meet rising demand. A special form of DRAM called high bandwidth memory (HBM) is the main memory driver, as graphics processing units (GPUs) need to be packaged with the chips to optimize their performance; otherwise, these super-expensive chips sit around idle way too long. The big three DRAM manufacturers are pouring most of their resources into HBM, but the companies are struggling to keep pace. One of the biggest reasons for this is that these companies are competing for the same extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems needed to make advanced logic chips, like GPUs and CPUs, and there is only one company in the world, ASML , that makes these machines. On top of that, HBM uses upward of 3 times the wafer capacity as ordinary DRAM, and it also takes years to build out new cleanrooms. Micron bulls argue that the HBM story makes the stock a buy, but it actually misses the point of what has been driving the company's performance. Micron actually derives only a small percentage of its revenue from HBM, likely less than 10%. It has the smallest HBM share in the market, at around 18% in Q2, in what is projected to be around a $55 billion market in 2026. Instead, Micron's revenue and margins are being driven by the surge in conventional DRAM and NAND prices, which have actually been rising faster than HBM prices. The problem is that if and when conventional memory prices normalize over the next several years, Micron's earnings could collapse. That is why SpaceX is the better long-term bet, despite Micron trading at a much cheaper valuation on the surface. Geoffrey Seiler has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. extraction.body: Europe's top technology official said the bloc's existing artificial intelligence framework is robust enough to manage worst-case scenarios involving highly capable autonomous systems, pushing back against calls from some industry leaders to slow the pace of frontier model development. Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's executive vice president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, told Reuters on Friday that the EU's AI Act was designed to address safety and security risks across the full lifecycle of advanced models, not merely at the point of deployment. Her comments come at a moment when global anxiety over "rogue" AI agents — systems that could act beyond human control — has intensified following high-profile incidents at companies including OpenAI and Anthropic. "We see that the safety and security of very capable models is a very hot topic internationally and we in Europe are well equipped for that," Virkkunen said in the interview. The AI Act, adopted two years ago as the first comprehensive legal framework of its kind, classifies systems according to risk level and imposes obligations ranging from transparency requirements to outright prohibitions on certain high-risk uses. Virkkunen's central argument is that the regulation's lifecycle-based structure gives European regulators a foundation to evaluate safety considerations from development through ongoing operation, rather than treating compliance as a one-time checkpoint before launch. Her confidence stands in direct contrast to warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who argued in a recent blog post that the speed of AI progress could "outrun our ability to understand and control these systems." Amodei pointed to recursive self-improvement — AI's growing capacity to build the next generation of AI — as a key driver of that acceleration. The divergence reflects a fundamental split in AI governance: whether risk should be managed primarily through regulatory structure and evidence-based safeguards, or whether the pace of development itself needs to be constrained. Virkkunen pushed back on critics who contend Europe's rules have already become outdated. She pointed to active implementation work, including regulatory guidance on model evaluation that incorporates recommendations from 60 AI experts. That detail signals Brussels is attempting to translate broad legal principles into concrete, testable evaluation practices — an area that frequently becomes a sticking point when new rules confront rapidly evolving technology. The Commission's supervisory posture is already visible in practice. In late August, regulators requested safety and security information from more than 30 unnamed AI companies, and Virkkunen said she is now assessing those responses. While she did not specify what actions might follow — whether additional guidance, enforcement proceedings, or policy adjustments — the information-gathering itself indicates an active oversight stance rather than a wait-and-see approach. For developers and investors, the immediate question is how the Commission's review will translate into clearer expectations for model evaluation, particularly around documenting safeguards relevant to autonomous or semi-autonomous behavior. The EU's position suggests that companies operating in European markets should plan compliance strategies around the existing framework rather than anticipating near-term legislative changes targeting advanced AI risks specifically. Separately, the U.S. Department of Justice is examining whether Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lived up to the terms of its landmark 2023 guilty plea agreement, according to multiple reports. The review centers on compliance with the settlement reached in November 2023, when the exchange admitted to anti-money laundering and sanctions violations and agreed to pay roughly $4.3 billion in penalties. Some reporting indicates the scrutiny is tied to a probe focused on possible Iran sanctions breaches — whether the exchange processed transactions that should have been blocked under U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control restrictions during the monitored period. Iran-linked activity was a core component of the original case against Binance, making sanctions compliance central to the settlement's framework. The 2023 resolution also forced Changpeng Zhao, the company's founder, to step down as chief executive and later plead guilty to a personal charge. The agreement placed Binance under an independent compliance monitor for a multi-year term, with ongoing obligations to restructure internal controls, train staff, file required reports, and cut off prohibited customers. A compliance review is not the same as a new enforcement action. The DOJ has not publicly announced charges or alleged a specific breach. What prosecutors have signaled is that Binance's post-settlement conduct warrants active examination — a distinction that carries serious consequences if the review surfaces violations. Any confirmed finding of non-compliance could trigger enhanced penalties, extended monitoring, or new restrictions on the exchange's U.S. operations. The exchange has not issued a detailed public comment addressing the specific allegations under review. Binance has continued to make compliance-related changes since the settlement, including ending direct crypto deposits to funding accounts and adding stricter identification requirements in certain markets, such as requiring transfer details for cross-border crypto transactions in Brazil starting November 1. Whether those changes satisfy the DOJ's settlement terms is precisely what the review appears to be examining. For the broader crypto sector, the DOJ's willingness to revisit a settled case sends a direct message: compliance obligations do not expire at signing. The review's outcome could also shape how other regulators assess major exchanges operating under U.S. regulatory shadows, and any enforcement action against Binance would be closely watched by the institutional investor base that has poured roughly $50 billion into crypto this year, according to JPMorgan. Tether's Brief THORChain Freeze Exposes Structural Tension In a separate development that underscores the friction between centralized stablecoin issuers and decentralized protocols, Tether temporarily blacklisted four THORChain vault addresses holding approximately $1.45 million in USDT on the Tron network, disrupting part of the cross-chain protocol's operations before removing the restrictions hours later without a publicly disclosed explanation. THORChain technical co-founder Chad Barraford said the protocol received no advance communication from Tether before the addresses were restricted. He initially said the team was trying to determine whether the action resulted from an error or misunderstanding, then later confirmed the addresses had been unfrozen and trading would resume. The funds remained in the vault addresses throughout the episode; the restriction prevented the affected USDT from being transferred while the addresses were on Tether's blacklist. The incident highlights a structural limit to decentralized finance systems that rely on centrally administered stablecoins. THORChain can decentralize vault control among validators through threshold signatures, but it cannot remove Tether's ability to freeze USDT at the token-contract level. Even when custody is decentralized, a centralized stablecoin issuer can determine whether its tokens remain transferable. On-chain analyst Khal noted that the vaults were blacklisted within the same three-block window as about 30 other wallets, suggesting the freeze "looks like collateral damage and not intentional." Tether has not publicly identified what triggered the temporary blacklist. The episode follows several recent disputes involving Tether's freeze authority. Cross-border payments company Conduit Technology sued Tether on October 5 over $2.76 million in USDT that it says has remained frozen since September 2025. Two Thai businessmen separately sued Tether in August over approximately $42.4 million in frozen USDT, alleging their addresses were restricted before U.S. authorities obtained a seizure warrant. Tether said earlier this year it has worked with more than 340 law-enforcement agencies across 65 countries and has frozen billions of dollars in USDT connected to sanctions, fraud and other alleged illicit activity. For DeFi protocols, the key risk is not simply freezing itself but uncertainty over what can trigger issuer intervention and how quickly legitimate holders can obtain review or reversal. The immediate disruption ended when Tether removed the four addresses from its blacklist, but the larger question remains unresolved because neither side has publicly explained why the vaults were selected in the first place. extraction.body: Europe's top technology official said the bloc's existing artificial intelligence framework is robust enough to manage worst-case scenarios involving highly capable autonomous systems, pushing back against calls from some industry leaders to slow the pace of frontier model development. Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's executive vice president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, told Reuters on Friday that the EU's AI Act was designed to address safety and security risks across the full lifecycle of advanced models, not merely at the point of deployment. Her comments come at a moment when global anxiety over "rogue" AI agents — systems that could act beyond human control — has intensified following high-profile incidents at companies including OpenAI and Anthropic. "We see that the safety and security of very capable models is a very hot topic internationally and we in Europe are well equipped for that," Virkkunen said in the interview. The AI Act, adopted two years ago as the first comprehensive legal framework of its kind, classifies systems according to risk level and imposes obligations ranging from transparency requirements to outright prohibitions on certain high-risk uses. Virkkunen's central argument is that the regulation's lifecycle-based structure gives European regulators a foundation to evaluate safety considerations from development through ongoing operation, rather than treating compliance as a one-time checkpoint before launch. Her confidence stands in direct contrast to warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who argued in a recent blog post that the speed of AI progress could "outrun our ability to understand and control these systems." Amodei pointed to recursive self-improvement — AI's growing capacity to build the next generation of AI — as a key driver of that acceleration. The divergence reflects a fundamental split in AI governance: whether risk should be managed primarily through regulatory structure and evidence-based safeguards, or whether the pace of development itself needs to be constrained. Virkkunen pushed back on critics who contend Europe's rules have already become outdated. She pointed to active implementation work, including regulatory guidance on model evaluation that incorporates recommendations from 60 AI experts. That detail signals Brussels is attempting to translate broad legal principles into concrete, testable evaluation practices — an area that frequently becomes a sticking point when new rules confront rapidly evolving technology. The Commission's supervisory posture is already visible in practice. In late August, regulators requested safety and security information from more than 30 unnamed AI companies, and Virkkunen said she is now assessing those responses. While she did not specify what actions might follow — whether additional guidance, enforcement proceedings, or policy adjustments — the information-gathering itself indicates an active oversight stance rather than a wait-and-see approach. For developers and investors, the immediate question is how the Commission's review will translate into clearer expectations for model evaluation, particularly around documenting safeguards relevant to autonomous or semi-autonomous behavior. The EU's position suggests that companies operating in European markets should plan compliance strategies around the existing framework rather than anticipating near-term legislative changes targeting advanced AI risks specifically. Separately, the U.S. Department of Justice is examining whether Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lived up to the terms of its landmark 2023 guilty plea agreement, according to multiple reports. The review centers on compliance with the settlement reached in November 2023, when the exchange admitted to anti-money laundering and sanctions violations and agreed to pay roughly $4.3 billion in penalties. Some reporting indicates the scrutiny is tied to a probe focused on possible Iran sanctions breaches — whether the exchange processed transactions that should have been blocked under U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control restrictions during the monitored period. Iran-linked activity was a core component of the original case against Binance, making sanctions compliance central to the settlement's framework. The 2023 resolution also forced Changpeng Zhao, the company's founder, to step down as chief executive and later plead guilty to a personal charge. The agreement placed Binance under an independent compliance monitor for a multi-year term, with ongoing obligations to restructure internal controls, train staff, file required reports, and cut off prohibited customers. A compliance review is not the same as a new enforcement action. The DOJ has not publicly announced charges or alleged a specific breach. What prosecutors have signaled is that Binance's post-settlement conduct warrants active examination — a distinction that carries serious consequences if the review surfaces violations. Any confirmed finding of non-compliance could trigger enhanced penalties, extended monitoring, or new restrictions on the exchange's U.S. operations. The exchange has not issued a detailed public comment addressing the specific allegations under review. Binance has continued to make compliance-related changes since the settlement, including ending direct crypto deposits to funding accounts and adding stricter identification requirements in certain markets, such as requiring transfer details for cross-border crypto transactions in Brazil starting November 1. Whether those changes satisfy the DOJ's settlement terms is precisely what the review appears to be examining. For the broader crypto sector, the DOJ's willingness to revisit a settled case sends a direct message: compliance obligations do not expire at signing. The review's outcome could also shape how other regulators assess major exchanges operating under U.S. regulatory shadows, and any enforcement action against Binance would be closely watched by the institutional investor base that has poured roughly $50 billion into crypto this year, according to JPMorgan. Tether's Brief THORChain Freeze Exposes Structural Tension In a separate development that underscores the friction between centralized stablecoin issuers and decentralized protocols, Tether temporarily blacklisted four THORChain vault addresses holding approximately $1.45 million in USDT on the Tron network, disrupting part of the cross-chain protocol's operations before removing the restrictions hours later without a publicly disclosed explanation. THORChain technical co-founder Chad Barraford said the protocol received no advance communication from Tether before the addresses were restricted. He initially said the team was trying to determine whether the action resulted from an error or misunderstanding, then later confirmed the addresses had been unfrozen and trading would resume. The funds remained in the vault addresses throughout the episode; the restriction prevented the affected USDT from being transferred while the addresses were on Tether's blacklist. The incident highlights a structural limit to decentralized finance systems that rely on centrally administered stablecoins. THORChain can decentralize vault control among validators through threshold signatures, but it cannot remove Tether's ability to freeze USDT at the token-contract level. Even when custody is decentralized, a centralized stablecoin issuer can determine whether its tokens remain transferable. On-chain analyst Khal noted that the vaults were blacklisted within the same three-block window as about 30 other wallets, suggesting the freeze "looks like collateral damage and not intentional." Tether has not publicly identified what triggered the temporary blacklist. The episode follows several recent disputes involving Tether's freeze authority. Cross-border payments company Conduit Technology sued Tether on October 5 over $2.76 million in USDT that it says has remained frozen since September 2025. Two Thai businessmen separately sued Tether in August over approximately $42.4 million in frozen USDT, alleging their addresses were restricted before U.S. authorities obtained a seizure warrant. Tether said earlier this year it has worked with more than 340 law-enforcement agencies across 65 countries and has frozen billions of dollars in USDT connected to sanctions, fraud and other alleged illicit activity. For DeFi protocols, the key risk is not simply freezing itself but uncertainty over what can trigger issuer intervention and how quickly legitimate holders can obtain review or reversal. The immediate disruption ended when Tether removed the four addresses from its blacklist, but the larger question remains unresolved because neither side has publicly explained why the vaults were selected in the first place. sources.title: AI is automating coding. So why are software developer job postings on the rise? - CNBC
passages: Some economic experts are pointing to the rebound in software job postings as confirmation for a glass half-full view of AI and the job market.

"It wasn't that long ago that we were reading the headline that there will be no more need for software developers," Eric Kutcher, North America chair at McKinsey, said during a recent interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Instead, he said, as companies are producing more code than ever before, software developers who work with AI remain in high demand.
"We're seeing much more growth in the places we thought we were gonna see the biggest displacement," Kutcher said.

Stanford University's 2026 AI index found that employment in AI-exposed fields for those aged 22 to 25 has fallen 16% since the rise of generative AI, with those identified as early-career software developers seeing a larger decline in employment of 20% as older developer roles expand.

U.S. software development job postings have risen since February 2025, the launch date for Anthropic's Claude Code, even as overall job postings fell, complicating predictions that AI would rapidly erase demand for developers.

While in recent years AI has been automating software-development tasks, the rebound comes after a steep drop from a 2022 hiring peak, when technology companies pulled back after a pandemic-era surge in hiring.
Indeed Hiring Lab found that senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase in software-development postings between May 2025 and May 2026.
Right now, factors like the ones cited by Puri are helping software developers to be among winners in the earliest stage of the AI transformation of the labor market.

extraction.body: U.S. software development job postings have risen since February 2025, the launch date for Anthropic's Claude Code, even as overall job postings fell, complicating predictions that AI would rapidly erase demand for developers. Concerns about the future of the software development career are well-founded, and intensified as companies adopted AI-powered coding tools, especially as those tools keep getting better. As far back as 2023, Microsoft's software development platform GitHub said that on projects where AI was available, it was close to writing half of all code. Some AI experts claim AI-written code across the entire GitHub platform has now passed the halfway mark . GitHub has not confirmed that, but in October it did report that one in three "pull requests" — the process in which coders that collaborate on development propose code changes for projects — now involve an AI agent. A year ago, GitHub said that number was fewer than one in 10. "If that pace holds, within the next two years, most of the code pushed to GitHub could be written by an agent. Much of it may never be fully read by a human," it stated . Labor market researchers say that against this backdrop, the profession is evolving rather than disappearing. Data from Indeed Hiring Lab shows that U.S. software-development job postings have risen nearly 15% since February 2025, bucking both the overall job market and the coding data. Some economic experts are pointing to the rebound in software job postings as confirmation for a glass half-full view of AI and the job market. "It wasn't that long ago that we were reading the headline that there will be no more need for software developers," Eric Kutcher, North America chair at McKinsey, said during a recent interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Instead, he said, as companies are producing more code than ever before, software developers who work with AI remain in high demand. "We're seeing much more growth in the places we thought we were gonna see the biggest displacement," Kutcher said. Recent research on AI and the future of jobs from McKinsey Global Institute notes that the earlier decline in the software developer field was not solely an AI story. While in recent years AI has been automating software-development tasks, the rebound comes after a steep drop from a 2022 hiring peak, when technology companies pulled back after a pandemic-era surge in hiring. But even after the recovery, software-development job postings remain about 27.5% below their pre-pandemic level, according to Indeed Hiring Lab data . Importantly, the increase is concentrated in senior-level roles and more experienced AI-oriented positions. Indeed Hiring Lab found that senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase in software-development postings between May 2025 and May 2026. Job titles that mention AI accounted for 37% of the increase. AI tools may be allowing companies to produce code more quickly than developers could on their own. GitHub leaders have said in the past that as much if not more than 80% of code could eventually be written by AI, especially as developers become more comfortable working with AI tools. But that also could mean the demand for workers is concentrated on those who can evaluate AI-generated code or problems and connect new tools to an organization's broader technology systems. Sneha Puri, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said companies are realizing that even if AI can handle some technical coding tasks, they still need developers to oversee that work, refine products and help clients integrate the technology into their day to day operations. One example, she said, is the growing need for workers who can help businesses apply AI tools beyond simply building them. Right now, factors like the ones cited by Puri are helping software developers to be among winners in the earliest stage of the AI transformation of the labor market. A recent analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data from economist Steve Rattner found that software developer was among the career categories that showed positive growth from May 2023 to May 2025, though it was merely in line with growth across all occupation and well below the pace of growth in traditionally blue-collar jobs associated with building AI data centers. Anthropic researchers found that even with automation, humans are still needed to oversee that automation and require user input. But the researchers cautioned that it is "by no means certain that this pattern will persist into the future." GitHub said in its report on pull requests that the as AI pushed more code into the world, and with it, more risks in the code, humans must be in a position to scale with the technology to police the AI's work. But that may not be possible forever. "As the amount of code grows, we must prevent more exposures and reduce the human effort required by those that remain, or else the volume of vulnerabilities introduced will become untenable," it wrote. For the youngest workers, the software development field outlook remains uncertain. Stanford University's 2026 AI index found that employment in AI-exposed fields for those aged 22 to 25 has fallen 16% since the rise of generative AI, with those identified as early-career software developers seeing a larger decline in employment of 20% as older developer roles expand. That shift has made the path into software development more difficult for recent graduates, even as demand rises for more experienced workers. Puri said students should build familiarity with AI tools but not neglect the skills that remain central when working with them. "Being able to use AI in your work and improve your efficiency is a great place to start," Puri said. "But communication, interpersonal skills and leadership are also really important," she added. Puri said employers also have a role to play in preserving routes into the field. "Today's entry-level talent becomes tomorrow's senior experts," she said. "If employers don't build those pipelines now, they're not going to have senior talent they need 10 years down the line." While forecasting job growth in the AI era is difficult, the long-term outlook for software developers remains positive, according to an August report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. It projects employment of software developers will grow 10% from 2025 to 2035, increasing from about 1.72 million to 1.89 million jobs and adding roughly 174,700 positions. extraction.body: U.S. software development job postings have risen since February 2025, the launch date for Anthropic's Claude Code, even as overall job postings fell, complicating predictions that AI would rapidly erase demand for developers. Concerns about the future of the software development career are well-founded, and intensified as companies adopted AI-powered coding tools, especially as those tools keep getting better. As far back as 2023, Microsoft's software development platform GitHub said that on projects where AI was available, it was close to writing half of all code. Some AI experts claim AI-written code across the entire GitHub platform has now passed the halfway mark . GitHub has not confirmed that, but in October it did report that one in three "pull requests" — the process in which coders that collaborate on development propose code changes for projects — now involve an AI agent. A year ago, GitHub said that number was fewer than one in 10. "If that pace holds, within the next two years, most of the code pushed to GitHub could be written by an agent. Much of it may never be fully read by a human," it stated . Labor market researchers say that against this backdrop, the profession is evolving rather than disappearing. Data from Indeed Hiring Lab shows that U.S. software-development job postings have risen nearly 15% since February 2025, bucking both the overall job market and the coding data. Some economic experts are pointing to the rebound in software job postings as confirmation for a glass half-full view of AI and the job market. "It wasn't that long ago that we were reading the headline that there will be no more need for software developers," Eric Kutcher, North America chair at McKinsey, said during a recent interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Instead, he said, as companies are producing more code than ever before, software developers who work with AI remain in high demand. "We're seeing much more growth in the places we thought we were gonna see the biggest displacement," Kutcher said. Recent research on AI and the future of jobs from McKinsey Global Institute notes that the earlier decline in the software developer field was not solely an AI story. While in recent years AI has been automating software-development tasks, the rebound comes after a steep drop from a 2022 hiring peak, when technology companies pulled back after a pandemic-era surge in hiring. But even after the recovery, software-development job postings remain about 27.5% below their pre-pandemic level, according to Indeed Hiring Lab data . Importantly, the increase is concentrated in senior-level roles and more experienced AI-oriented positions. Indeed Hiring Lab found that senior roles accounted for 71% of the increase in software-development postings between May 2025 and May 2026. Job titles that mention AI accounted for 37% of the increase. AI tools may be allowing companies to produce code more quickly than developers could on their own. GitHub leaders have said in the past that as much if not more than 80% of code could eventually be written by AI, especially as developers become more comfortable working with AI tools. But that also could mean the demand for workers is concentrated on those who can evaluate AI-generated code or problems and connect new tools to an organization's broader technology systems. Sneha Puri, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said companies are realizing that even if AI can handle some technical coding tasks, they still need developers to oversee that work, refine products and help clients integrate the technology into their day to day operations. One example, she said, is the growing need for workers who can help businesses apply AI tools beyond simply building them. Right now, factors like the ones cited by Puri are helping software developers to be among winners in the earliest stage of the AI transformation of the labor market. A recent analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data from economist Steve Rattner found that software developer was among the career categories that showed positive growth from May 2023 to May 2025, though it was merely in line with growth across all occupation and well below the pace of growth in traditionally blue-collar jobs associated with building AI data centers. Anthropic researchers found that even with automation, humans are still needed to oversee that automation and require user input. But the researchers cautioned that it is "by no means certain that this pattern will persist into the future." GitHub said in its report on pull requests that the as AI pushed more code into the world, and with it, more risks in the code, humans must be in a position to scale with the technology to police the AI's work. But that may not be possible forever. "As the amount of code grows, we must prevent more exposures and reduce the human effort required by those that remain, or else the volume of vulnerabilities introduced will become untenable," it wrote. For the youngest workers, the software development field outlook remains uncertain. Stanford University's 2026 AI index found that employment in AI-exposed fields for those aged 22 to 25 has fallen 16% since the rise of generative AI, with those identified as early-career software developers seeing a larger decline in employment of 20% as older developer roles expand. That shift has made the path into software development more difficult for recent graduates, even as demand rises for more experienced workers. Puri said students should build familiarity with AI tools but not neglect the skills that remain central when working with them. "Being able to use AI in your work and improve your efficiency is a great place to start," Puri said. "But communication, interpersonal skills and leadership are also really important," she added. Puri said employers also have a role to play in preserving routes into the field. "Today's entry-level talent becomes tomorrow's senior experts," she said. "If employers don't build those pipelines now, they're not going to have senior talent they need 10 years down the line." While forecasting job growth in the AI era is difficult, the long-term outlook for software developers remains positive, according to an August report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. It projects employment of software developers will grow 10% from 2025 to 2035, increasing from about 1.72 million to 1.89 million jobs and adding roughly 174,700 positions. passages: The major artificial intelligence companies’ prime directive to literally bulldoze AI infrastructure into states with minimal regulation has produced citizen-led, bipartisan demands for local and national moratoriums on data center siting.

While the Trump administration is doing everything it can to facilitate the only capital spending with a pulse in the economy, these calls for moratoriums are growing, and connecting with local successes in blocking data center construction.
Elsewhere in Michigan, data center opponents rallied in Lansing last week and called for “ no secret deals ” between local governments, utilities, and data center developers.
Power demand from data centers will hit 106 gigawatts by 2035 , according to an analysis from BloombergNEF.

A Yale Clean Energy Forum report estimates that data centers could take up as much as 12 percent of total U.S. power consumption by 2028, a higher demand than all manufacturing of steel, aluminum, and other high-intensity manufactured goods combined.

Illinois also has one of the highest concentrations of data centers in the country, and local officials and environmentalists have raised alarms that siting decisions don’t always take into consideration how local drinking water needs can clash with data center cooling demands.

The data center developer for Project Jupiter, a multibillion-dollar component of the $500 billion SoftBank- and OpenAI-led Stargate Project, got to know the locals, but the underlying clients remained unknown because county officials had signed NDAs.

Combine data center moratorium drama with the gutting of the Affordable Care Act, the nothing-to-see-here response to the affordability crisis, and extortionate trade tactics, and the White House and congressional Republicans have set themselves and everyone else up for a very dismal New Year.
